Agent runtime infra: agent UI protocols & durable agent execution — AG-UI event streams and A2UI declarative UI, SSE/WebSocket fan-out at scale, human-in-the-loop interrupts, durable runs with checkpointed state and resume after node loss

Agent runtime infra: agent identity & delegated authorization — per-agent workload identity, OAuth on-behalf-of and token exchange, short-lived scoped tool credentials, step-up approvals for risky actions, and fleet-wide agent kill switches

Agent runtime infra: hosting coding agents for an org — Claude Code, Codex, OpenHands, Goose and Gemini CLI fleets, harnesses and Agent Skills distribution, per-repo credential scoping, model-gateway budgets and auditing agent-authored changes

Agent runtime infra: multi-agent orchestration & workflow builders as platform services — multi-tenant Dify, n8n, Langflow and Flowise, Mastra/Deer Flow-style orchestration, plugin and node supply-chain risk, secrets in workflows, and blast-radius limits for agent swarms

Agent runtime infra capstone: designing an agent platform for 10K concurrent agents — gateway, memory, sandbox, browser and observability layers on Kubernetes/GPU cells, capacity math, SLOs, cost per agent task and the security review

Not a CUDA-kernel course.

agent_infra_landscape.note: Agent runtime infrastructure track (Lessons 52-61), added at Rohit's request from the 'Agent Infra Landscape 2026' map. Focus on the bottom 'Agent Runtime Infra' layer: memory/knowledge/context (OpenViking, Milvus, RAGFlow, Cognee, Hindsight, Headroom, mem0, Supermemory, seekdb), protocols/interop (A2UI, IBM MCP ContextForge, AgentGateway, ToolHive, MCP, AG-UI, A2A, Agent Skills), tools/web/computer use (Lark CLI, CUA, Agent Browser, Firecrawl, Browser Use, page-agent), dev sandboxes (Coder, kubernetes-sigs Agent Sandbox, OpenSandbox, Daytona), observability/eval (Langfuse, Opik, Arize Phoenix, promptfoo). Write from a platform/SRE/security view of running these at fleet scale on Kubernetes and GPU cells. Build on Lessons 30-34 (data, eval, LLM judge, prompt/tool catalog, agent sandboxing/egress) and 48 (workload identity) instead of repeating them. Keep all house requirements; the Security & hardening section adapts weights/checkpoints/registries/signing/bucket IAM/secure deployments to agents: tool credentials, prompt injection, egress, memory poisoning, signed MCP servers/skills/sandbox images.
